topic: Does a drink warm you up when you are freezing?
title: A Drink In The Cold
idea: Alcohol makes you feel warm while your body loses heat faster.
hook: You're freezing. Does a drink warm you, or cool you?

beats.line: One sip, and a warm glow spreads through you.
beats.see: Hero shivers in a snowy tent, takes a sip from a flask; an orange glow spreads over the cutout body on 'glow'. Cards A/B shrink to the corner.

beats.line: That glow is blood rushing out to your skin.
beats.see: X-ray view: red vessels near the skin widen like opening pipes on 'rushing', blood flows outward on 'skin'.

beats.line: So it's card B. It feels warm while you lose heat.
beats.see: Card B gets a check on 'B'; heat waves float off the skin into the cold air, a body thermometer slides down on 'lose'.

beats.line: A lot of alcohol can also weaken shivering, your heater.
beats.see: Shivering motion lines around the hero shrink on 'weaken'; a small paper heater icon inside his chest flickers on 'heater'.

beats.line: Below about eighty six degrees inside your body, shivering stops.
beats.see: Core thermometer drops to 86°F on 'eighty six'; the shiver lines vanish completely on 'stops', frost creeps in.

beats.line: One. Put something between you and the frozen ground.
beats.see: Step card 1 INSULATE; hero lifts off the ice onto a foam pad and backpack on 'Put', cold arrows from the ground get blocked.

beats.line: Two. Cover your head and neck, and get out of the wind.
beats.see: Step card 2 COVER UP; hat and scarf snap on at 'Cover', a wind gust bounces off the tent wall on 'wind'.

beats.line: Three. Stay dry, and eat something warm and full of calories.
beats.see: Step card 3 STAY DRY, EAT; wet socks swapped for dry on 'dry', a steaming bowl of soup appears on 'warm', calorie flames rise from it.

end.line: Picked warms you? That warm feeling is your heat leaving.
end.see: Cards A and B return big; A flips to show the glowing hero with heat waves streaming off him on 'leaving'.

description: You're freezing and someone hands you a drink. Does it warm you up or cool you down?

facts.claim: Alcohol widens blood vessels in the skin: it gives a sensation of warmth but increases heat loss.
Larger doses of alcohol can impair shivering; shivering is how the body makes heat.
facts.source: Kalant & Le 1983, PubMed 6144116 ; Wilderness Medical Society guideline via AAFP https://www.aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2020/1101/p571.html

facts.claim: Shivering stops near 30 C core temperature (= 86 F).
Insulate from the ground, cover head and neck, stay dry and out of the wind, eat warm high-calorie food.

notes: Correct card: B (COOLS YOU). Weakest-evidence topic: no 'drops your temperature by X'; shivering line uses 'a lot of' + 'can' per FACTS. 86 F is a straight conversion of the FACTS '30 C' (shivering stops near 30 C); the number is about hypothermia in general, not an alcohol effect, and the script does not claim alcohol causes it. Alcohol and a 13+ audience: framing is purely 'it doesn't help'; no drinking shown as positive. St. Bernard barrel left out.
